definition: The Packrat parser is a type of parser that shares similarities with the recursive descent parser in its construction.
details: However, it differs because it takes parsing expression grammars (PEGs) as input rather than LL grammars. In 1970, Alexander Birman laid the groundwork for packrat parsing by introducing the "TMG recognition scheme" (TS), and "generalized TS" (gTS). TS was based upon Robert M. McClure's TMG compiler-compiler, and gTS was based upon Dewey Val Schorre's META compiler-compiler. Birman's work was later refined by Aho and Ullman; and renamed as Top-Down Parsing Language (TDPL), and Generalized TDPL (GTDPL), respectively. These algorithms were the first of their kind to employ deterministic top-down parsing with backtracking. Bryan Ford developed PEGs as an expansion of GTDPL and TS. Unlike CFGs, PEGs are unambiguous and can match well with machine-oriented languages. PEGs, similar to GTDPL and TS, can also express all LL(k) and LR(k). Ford also introduced Packrat as a parser that uses memoization techniques on top of a simple PEG parser. This was done because PEGs have an unlimited lookahead capability resulting in a parser with exponential time performance in the worst case. explainer.lead: A packrat parser is a parser built like a recursive descent parser but taking parsing expression grammars as input rather than LL grammars. Its lineage traces back to Birman's TMG recognition scheme, later refined into TDPL.

tiers.eli5: It is a reader that, instead of re-reading the same passage, remembers what it already worked out and reuses it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use packrat parsing for PEG-based grammars, benefiting from its memoization approach. A pitfall is the memory cost of remembering results for every position and rule.
tiers.paperLevel: A packrat parser shares recursive descent construction but consumes parsing expression grammars instead of LL grammars; its groundwork was Birman's TMG recognition scheme and generalized TS, later refined by Aho and Ullman as TDPL and generalized TDPL.

explainer.example: A parser for a PEG-based configuration language applies packrat parsing to handle the grammar without backtracking repeatedly.
